newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trading slows late Tuesday -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trading slows late Tuesday -trade.

text.p: Cattle trading was slow late Tuesday after active sales early in the day at $63.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Nearly 25,000 head traded in Kansas early Tuesday, mostly at $63.00. By late morning meat packers reduced bids to $62.00 and $62.50 from Texas to Kansas but feedlots passed.
"It's not buying anything," a Texas feedlot source said of the lower bids. "I'm not sure $63.00 would buy anything with the futures closing the way they did."
CME June live cattle futures closed up 0.575 cent at 64.025 cents per lb and August was up 0.350 at 63.525.
At $63.00, feedlots probably covered the cost of feeding cattle that were placed as young calves, but lost $10 to $35 per head on cattle placed on feed as yearlings, sources said.
A few cattle feeders said Tuesday's sales exhausted their showlists, but others still had cattle to sell.

USDA as of mid-afternoon put cattle sales in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area at 15,100 and the week-to-date total there at 63,300 head. Kansas sales as of mid-afternoon totaled 42,100 head and week-to-date sales were pegged at 52,800 by USDA.
